claims.claim: DIDS-MFL achieves competitive binary intrusion detection on NF-UNSW-NB15-v2
DIDS-MFL improves detection consistency on previously-unseen (unknown) attacks
claims.value: Mean detection recall on the 9 leave-one-attack-out hidden attacks: DIDS-MFL 0.969, E-GraphSAGE 0.959, MLP 0.951; subset F1 0.678 vs 0.677 / 0.667

claims.claim: DIDS-MFL delivers the highest, and most stable, few-shot binary detection recall on rare attacks (Analysis, Backdoor, Fuzzers, Shellcode, Worms)
claims.value: Mean binary recall = 0.9812 for k in {1,5,10,50}, vs E-GraphSAGE 0.949–0.959, MLP 0.965–0.981

claims.claim: Each module of DIDS-MFL contributes to performance
claims.value: Removing the representational disentangler drops binary F1 to 0.9844 (lowest among DIDS-MFL variants); removing multi-scale fusion drops multiclass macro F1 to 0.4658.
claims.caveat: Some ablation variants score slightly higher on a single metric due to seed variance; DIDS-MFL wins on the most stringent test (unknown / few-shot).

claims.claim: Disentanglement produces visibly better-separated attack clusters
Per-attack F1 confirms heterogeneous difficulty: Generic / Reconnaissance / Shellcode are well-detected; Backdoor / Worms / Analysis are still hard
